trace.final_message:
Added `snap_spans` in a new `hourglass/rounding.py`, with tests, and committed it on `master`. The commit is not pushed.

`snap_spans(spans, step_minutes)` returns one text label per span, in the order given. Each label is the start time, a dash, the end time, and then the length in hours and minutes in parentheses. Start and end are each rounded to the nearest multiple of the step, and exact halves round up.

Choices I made where the request was open:

- **Return type:** the function returns the labels only. It does not return the rounded spans, so a caller who needs the numbers would have to parse the labels. Say if you want the rounded spans returned as well.
- **Bad steps:** zero, negative, or a step that does not divide sixty evenly raises `ValueError`. The check runs before any span is read.
- **Collapsing spans:** if a span's rounded start and end land on the same time, it raises `ValueError` rather than producing an empty label. A short span near a step boundary would otherwise vanish from payroll without warning.
- **Length format:** the length always shows both parts, so an exact hour reads as zero minutes.

Tests: `tests/test_rounding.py` has eight tests covering rounding, half-up ties, a step of one, end of day, input order, empty input, bad steps, and collapsing spans. The full suite has thirty-four tests and all pass. Lint reports no syntax errors.

I also added a line to `CHANGES.txt` under Unreleased and an entry in `docs/api.txt`.

The project's main branch is `main`, but the commit went on `master`, which was the branch checked out. Say if you want it moved to a branch for review.

commits.message:
Add snap_spans for rounding spans to a fixed step

Labels each span with its start and end rounded to the nearest step, such as 09:00-17:15 (8h 15m). Steps that are zero, negative or do not divide an hour evenly raise ValueError, and a span that rounds to nothing also raises. Exact halves round up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

before.docs/api.txt:
hourglass.parsing.parse_clock(text): read a clock time as minutes since midnight
hourglass.parsing.format_clock(minutes): minutes since midnight as HH:MM
hourglass.parsing.parse_span(text): read a range such as 09:00-17:30
hourglass.parsing.format_span(span): a span as start-end text
hourglass.parsing.normalize_day(text): short lowercase day name
hourglass.merging.spans_overlap(first, second): whether two spans share any time
hourglass.merging.intersect_spans(first, second): the part two spans share
hourglass.merging.merge_spans(spans): collapse overlaps into a sorted list
hourglass.merging.total_minutes(spans): minutes covered, overlaps counted once
hourglass.schedule.parse_schedule_text(text): parse schedule CSV held in memory
hourglass.schedule.load_schedule(path): read a schedule CSV from disk
hourglass.schedule.shifts_for_worker(shifts, worker): all shifts for one worker
hourglass.schedule.worker_minutes(shifts): scheduled minutes per worker
hourglass.schedule.day_coverage(shifts, day): merged spans for a day
hourglass.schedule.format_day_line(shifts, day): one text line for a day
